title: Initial Outcomes of Physician-Modified Inner-Branched Endovascular Repair for Distal Aortic Arch Aneurysm
content: Background/Objectives: Although acceptable initial outcomes after physician-modified inner-branched endovascular repair (PMiBEVAR) for thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm have been reported, few clinical studies have reported on PMiBEVAR for aortic arch aneurysm. Herein, we evaluate the initial outcomes of six cases of proximal landing zone 2 PMiBEVAR. Methods: This retrospective study analyzed data from six patients who underwent zone 2 PMiBEVAR for aortic arch aneurysms at a single center between October 2021 and June 2024. The outcomes were 30-day mortality and postoperative complications. Results: The median follow-up period was 12.5 (7.3–25) months. The patients had a median age of 78.5 (76.5–79.0) years, and the median aneurysm diameter was 56 (50–61) mm. Technical success was achieved in 5/6 (83.3%) cases. The median modification and operative times were 56 (45–60) min and 92 (79–308), respectively. Open abdominal surgery was required in one patient due to access vessel bleeding. Postoperatively, delayed type Ia endoleak and vascular access-site complication occurred in one patient each. However, no patients experienced stroke, spinal cord ischemia, or other complications. The median hospital stay was 10 (7–41) days, and no deaths or reinterventions occurred after 30 days. During post-discharge follow-up, the aneurysm diameter remained “unchanged” in four patients, including the one with delayed type Ia endoleak, while two patients experienced aneurysm diameter shrinkage. Ultimately, one patient died due to respiratory failure. Conclusions: PMiBEVAR for distal aortic arch aneurysm might be effective in improving postoperative outcomes; however, further studies are required to confirm these results.
